_comment: Gemma 4's multi-token-prediction drafter (`Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM`, Google's `-it-assistant` repos). Unlike a Qwen3.5 head it ships as its own checkpoint with its own config, so it names its target config (`head_targets`: its stem -> `<arch>/<stem>`). Google publishes no target checkpoint that carries it: its drafter is always a repo of its own, which its model card loads by name (`assistant_model`). So the drafter a target drafts with by default names the repo each compiled variant of it loads from (`published_as`, a drafter checkpoint loading only into the variant of its own precision): it compiles beside its selected target under `mtp-heads` (on with `metal`), and serving a checkpoint of that target's shape with no `--speculative-model` loads that repo. 26B-A4B's is the QAT drafter's MLX 4-bit conversion: on the MLX 4-bit target (base M5, one request, 256 tokens, TPOT against the target alone's 21.0 ms) it reads 18.2 / 17.2 ms on a code prompt greedy / sampled and 20.6 / 20.2 on prose, its first token at the target's; Google's bf16 drafter, which accepts as many drafts, reads every draft's 262k-row lm_head at bf16 and loses on prose (26.5 / 25.8 ms) and pays its first token ~10 ms; the g32 conversion of it reads within 3% of the QAT one but needs its own preset. The others compile under `spec/mtp` and draft when `--speculative-model` names them. The target's facts it needs come from its `.overrides.json`: the target's layer count (its KV pool's geometry) and the target layers whose KV it reads. It has NO K/V of its own (`num_kv_shared_layers` = all its layers): its attention reads the target's KV of the target's last sliding and last full layer (`reads_target_kv`). It borrows only its target's embedding (`borrows`), placed under `target_embed_tokens`; its logits are its own tied 262k x 1024 embedding's, read as the `lm_head` linear straight from `model.embed_tokens` (renamed: the drafter never reads its embedding as one). `pre_projection` / `post_projection` sit at the checkpoint's top level (`top_level_weights`). mlx sets the attention `scale = 1.0` for both classes, as the target's. Rope scalars are nested per class under `rope_parameters`, aliased to the flat names as the target's.
